questions.q: Which three beats make up the narrative arc used in this lesson?
questions.explain: Setup gives shared context, tension shows what threatens the goal, and resolution names the action.

questions.q: Which chart title states a message rather than describing the chart?
questions.explain: A message title makes a specific, checkable claim. The others only say what the chart contains.

questions.q: You cannot write a clear message for one dashboard chart. What should you do?
options: Ask whether it belongs on the dashboard, or move it to a report
questions.explain: If a chart has no message, it is likely backup detail. Reports can hold it without cluttering the executive view.

questions.q: Which is an example of chartjunk?
options: A rainbow palette where the colors carry no meaning
A footer that defines win rate by count
A single accent color on the stalled deals
A title that states the takeaway
questions.explain: Chartjunk is decoration that carries no data. Meaningless color variety makes viewers hunt for a meaning that is not there.

questions.q: In native Salesforce dashboards, where can you carry annotation-like information?
options: Component titles, subtitles, footers and conditional colors on metric and gauge components
questions.explain: Native tools have limited annotation, so titles, subtitles, footers and threshold colors do the job. Tableau supports annotations directly on the view.
